Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:67058
Court No. - 73

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 4824 of 2024
Applicant :- Wajid Siddiqui

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Waseem Ahmad
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Istiyak Khan, learned Advocate, holding brief of Sri Waseem Ahmad, learned counsel for the applicant and Dr. S.B. Maurya, learned AGA-I for the State-respondent.
2.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
248 of 2023, under Sections 467, 468, 471 IPC, Police Station- Dhoomanganj Commissionarate,
District- Prayagraj, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3.Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that in the present matter earlier applicant was released on bail by this Court vide order dated 31.01.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 2545 of 2024 for the offences under Sections 420, 120-B I.P.C. and Section 3, 6 Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933, Section 4, 20, 21, 25 Indian Telegraphy (Amendment) Act 1885 and Section 66, 66D of Information and Technology Act, 2008 but during investigation offences under Section 467, 468 , 471 IPC were added and when he applied for bail for added offences before the court concerned then his bail application has been dismissed.
Wajid Siddiqui vs State Of U.P. on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38604332/
1 4.

sentences.text: He further submitted that after considering entire facts of the case, earlier this Court has enlarged the applicant on bail, therefore, for added offences, applicant should also be released on bail.
5. He further submitted that in the present matter, applicant is in jail since 22.05.2023 i.e. for almost a year.
6. Per contra, learned AGA however, opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
7. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. From the record, it reflects that in the present matter on 31.12.2024, this Court enlarged the applicant on bail for the offences under Sections 420, 120-B I.P.C. and Section 3, 6 Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933, Section 4, 20, 21, 25 Indian Telegraphy (Amendment) Act 1885 and Section 66, 66D of Information and Technology Act, 2008 but it appears that during investigation charge sheet was also filed for the offences under Sections 467, 468, 471 IPC.

It appears that the order dated 31.01.2024 passed by this Court is reasoned and detailed order and, therefore, this Court find force in the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is also entitled to be released on bail for the added offences, therefore, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

9. As vide order dated 31.01.2024, applicant has been released on bail in this case on his personal bond and two sureties, therefore, in the present matter, learned court concerned is directed to release the applicant on bail only on the basis of his personal bond.
10. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
11. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant- Wajid Siddiqui be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.

14. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
